The EU and Canada have concluded negotiations on a Digital Trade Agreement to modernise bilateral trade and complement CETA, provisionally applied since 2017.
The pact covers cross-border data flows, e-contracts, e-signatures, e-invoices and consumer protection rules.
EU-Canada goods and services trade rose 80 per cent from 2016 to 2025, the Commission said.

title: Germany's October inflation seen at 2.8%
summary:
Germany's annual inflation rate is expected to reach 2.8 per cent in October 2026, while consumer prices fell 0.2 per cent month on month, according to provisional Destatis data. 
Core inflation is forecast at 2.1 per cent, while energy prices rose 12.2 per cent year on year. 
HICP inflation is also expected at 2.8 per cent.

title: India extends cotton duty exemption until Dec 31; SIMA welcomes move
summary:
India has extended the cotton import duty exemption until December 31, 2026, amid a projected supply shortage. 
SIMA welcomed the move, saying it would help textile manufacturers secure raw materials and meet export commitments. 
The association urged the government to extend the exemption until 2030 to ensure supply and price stability.

title: China’s textile profits up 7.2%: Why are apparel-related profits down?
summary:
China’s textile-industry profits rose 7.2 per cent to ¥42.83 billion, with revenue up 1.7 per cent to ¥1,601.04 billion, NBS data released on October 28 show.
The broader manufacture of textile, wearing apparel and accessories category saw profits fall 15.6 per cent to ¥21.95 billion and revenue drop 4.2 per cent.
The figures do not establish separate fabric or garment margins.

title: Dutch economy grows 0.6% in Q3 on exports & consumption
summary:
The Dutch economy grew 0.6 per cent quarter on quarter in Q3 2026, driven by exports and consumption, while investment declined 0.1 per cent, according to CBS. 
Year on year, GDP rose 2.1 per cent, supported by household spending and the trade balance. 
Manufacturing made the largest sectoral contribution to quarterly growth.

title: India’s GDP growth estimated at 7.35% in Q2 FY27: Economic Review
summary:
India’s economic growth remained resilient in Q2 FY27, with GDP growth estimated at 7.35 per cent, supported by strong industrial activity, exports, investment and domestic demand, according to the October Economic Review. 
However, rising food and fuel inflation, global uncertainty and higher energy prices pose risks to growth and price stability in the coming months.

title: US' Avery Dennison's Q3 sales rise 5.2% to $2.33 bn
summary:
Avery Dennison reported third-quarter 2026 net sales of $2.33 billion, up 5.2 per cent year on year, as organic sales rose 3.7 per cent. 
Net income advanced 2 per cent to $169.7 million and adjusted diluted earnings per share rose 2.1 per cent to $2.42. 
Materials Group growth offset softer reported Solutions Group sales, while the US company expects FY26 adjusted EPS of $10.10-$10.24.

title: China & Switzerland sign optimised free trade accord
summary:
Switzerland and China today signed an optimised free trade agreement to ease trade and investment and improve Swiss goods and investment access.
It strengthens environmental and labour rules in a legally binding trade and sustainable development chapter.
Other deals cover labour and employment cooperation and research-data rules, as Parmelin leads a business and scientific delegation.

title: Bangladesh’s ESG platform: Can 327 factories win global buyers trust?
summary:
BGMEA has launched an ESG platform to publish factory-reported data from Bangladesh member factories and reduce duplicate information requests.
At launch, 326 factories had submitted data; the 2025–26 survey cohort covers 327 factories, about 13.1 per cent of 2,500 active members.
The platform does not replace buyer due diligence or audits, and mandatory reporting has no announced date.

title: Turkiye’s apparel exports decline 2.2% in first three quarters
summary:
Turkiye's apparel exports fell 2.23 per cent year on year to $12.044 billion in January–September 2026, with September shipments down 4.43 per cent to $1.377 billion.
Knitted and crocheted garments eased 1.5 per cent to $7.032 billion, while woven apparel fell 3.3 per cent to $5.012 billion.
Subdued European demand, cautious buying and price competition continue to pressure exporters.

title: Bangladesh’s EU apparel market: A changing export landscape?
summary:
Bangladesh’s EU RMG exports fell 11.67 per cent in January–August 2026 as market share slipped from 21.5 per cent to 19.8 per cent.
Spain overtook Germany in Q1 FY2026–27, with shipments up 13.73 per cent to $1.148 billion against Germany’s $1.123 billion.
Volumes fell 4.58 per cent and unit prices 7.43 per cent, while China and Vietnam gained ground ahead of Bangladesh’s LDC graduation.

title: Europe overtakes North America as Madagascar's top apparel market
summary:
Europe overtook North America as Madagascar’s top apparel export region in January–September 2026, even as total shipments fell 29.86 per cent YoY to $567.08 million.
Exports to Europe declined 17.95 per cent to $228.62 million, but its share rose to 40.32 per cent; North America plunged 41.93 per cent to $198.51 million.
US shipments fell 43.03 per cent amid tariff and AGOA uncertainty.

title: AAFA urges USTR to ease barriers for US apparel firms
summary:
AAFA has urged USTR to address trade barriers affecting US apparel, footwear and sewn-products companies across 12 markets, citing tariffs, customs delays, restrictive regulations and inconsistent enforcement. 
It cited $28.44 billion in US tariffs in 2025 and called for predictable tariffs, lower input duties and improved trade facilitation.

title: US' Crocs raises FY26 outlook as HeyDude returns to growth
summary:
Crocs has lifted its FY26 revenue growth outlook to about 3 per cent and adjusted diluted earnings per share guidance to $14.45-$14.65 after robust Q3 execution. 
Third-quarter revenue rose 4.6 per cent to $1.04 billion and net income increased 48.7 per cent to $216.8 million.  
HeyDude revenue climbed 6.1 per cent, returning to growth, while Crocs Brand international sales rose 11.8 per cent.

title: Turkiye’s apparel exports fall 9.3%: Is Egypt gaining more ground now?
summary:
Turkiye’s apparel exports (HS 61-62) fell 9.3 per cent to $10.60 billion in January-August 2026 from the same 2024 period as pressure rose on producers.
Textile exports across HS 50-60 were nearly flat at $7.94 billion, while apparel imports rose 28.8 per cent to $2.92 billion.
Orta Anadolu is closing Kayseri production facilities and TYH Tekstil remains in court-supervised concordat.

title: US apparel import values fall 7%: Why are retail prices still rising?
summary:
US apparel CPI rose 3.4 per cent in the year to September 2026, outpacing a 1.3 per cent rise in apparel manufacturing import prices.
The gain was nearly five times the 0.7 per cent rise in core goods, while headline inflation reached 3.7 per cent.
Imports under HS 61 and 62 fell 7.0 per cent by value in January-August, and exporters must factor July Section 301 duties into landed costs.

title: US' Columbia raises FY26 sales outlook after stronger Q3
summary:
Columbia Sportswear has raised the low end of its FY26 sales and diluted earnings per share outlook after a stronger-than-expected third quarter, supported by earlier wholesale shipments, improving US DTC trends and international momentum. 
Q3 net sales rose 2 per cent to $962.6 million and net income increased to $84.7 million from $52 million. 
Operating margin reached 11.4 per cent.

title: Why garment construction matters for apparel brand margins
summary:
Apparel brands can manage manufacturing costs by simplifying garment construction, though savings are limited if fabric use is unchanged.
Belinda Jacobs of Techpacks.co says complex seams, linings, pockets, speciality stitching and custom fasteners add labour across production runs.
She warns cutting stitching quality, seam allowances or reinforcement can raise defects, returns and hurt trust.

title: EU takes 49% of Bangladesh RMG exports: What happens after EBA?
summary:
Bangladesh’s EU EBA garment preferences could continue to end-2029 after its scheduled LDC graduation on November 24, 2026, or to end-2032 if the UN approves an extension.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1395 grants a three-year transition, but rules of origin will shape future apparel eligibility.
The EU took $19.06 billion, or 49.25 per cent, of Bangladesh’s FY2025–26 RMG exports.
